comment: Which issue owns a gap with libwebrtc (tools/parity_report.py). Rules match the scenario and metric with fnmatch patterns; every matching rule adds its issues. Keep it in step with the work list in roadmap issue #64 and the deviation inventory (docs/design/libwebrtc-parity.md). A gap with no owner needs an issue or an approved deviation. An owner counts only while its issue is open, or when its rule carries a note (the explanation of a closed, explained difference); closed issues in a rule without a note own nothing.

rules.note: In band on every cell, explained (#536, yardstick #792, #725): libwebrtc M157 behaves the same way at 20% random loss on a clean 2 Mbps link (pacer queue 1-2.5 s, A/V sync drags audio; m2e p95 728 vs ours 613 ms) and during a 45 s feedback-only outage (m2e p95 2070 vs 2059 ms). The Tester's stage-2 targets are a stage:later item.

D11 explained (#842): stuck-packet episodes in the 20 ms (1500 B) bottleneck queue, on both stacks, with timing set by the encoder target. Video and RTX leave at the same instant as an audio packet, so a packet larger than about 1280-1380 B can't pass the queue until a keyframe clears it, and whether a frame splits into such packets depends on its size (equal-size FU-A split: seed 1's keyframe at 10.03 s is 8 x 1448 B on ours, never delivered, and 9 x 1339 B on libwebrtc's, through by 11.71 s). The stack that has an episode around 20-25 s is still in LossBasedBweV2's kDecreasing/HOLD at the 25 s rise and settles late: ours earlier on 8/10 seeds after #837 (3580 vs 6020 ms), with no seed-wise correlation before it (5970 vs 5720). The rules involved are the same on both sides: LossBasedBweV2 candidates and constants, kMaxNackRetries, the RTT gating of resends, cwnd pushback (0 on both), a PLI after 3 s without a decodable frame (seed 2: 13.32 vs 13.72 s; seed 4: 15.56/18.56 vs 21.85/24.85 s, each 3 s into its own episode; libwebrtc sends none on seed 1 because its keyframe got through), and the pacer order audio > RTX > video (prioritized_packet_queue.cc). Yardstick #843: cwnd, LossBasedBweV2 state and PLI/FIR rows on seeds 1, 2 and 4.

#738 (yardstick #806, 40 seeds): GoogCC takes cwnd_reduce_ratio from the pushback target after the clamp to its minimum bitrate (goog_cc_network_control.cc:596-608), so once the pushback reaches the minimum the ratio stops changing and the reset to 0 of the 270p reconfiguration (AddObserver) holds; ours took it before the clamp. With the port (PR for #738), ours 20.1 % loss, 523 ms e2e p95, 365 ms A/V p95 against libwebrtc 20.4 %, 503 ms, 348 ms; the ~1 s mode on 15/40 seeds against libwebrtc 14/40 (main 26/40), and seed 2 matches libwebrtc to the millisecond (206 vs 205 ms).

A/V sync, explained (#504, Fixer trace on seed 1, #719): audio reaches the receiver 40-47 ms after capture on both stacks for the whole call, so NetEq sees no jitter; its target follows each stack's video delay through StreamSynchronization (video/stream_synchronization.cc:22, kMaxChangeMs 80). The video delay comes from each stack's CC run, owned by this scenario's video/CC owner.

Not a parity test: `apm_rate` is ours only (the APM modules built at an unsupported rate before the call, outside it) and sm_compare's libwebrtc side ignores it. Neither call runs APM, so what both sides run is a plain 5 s audio and video call on a clean 2 Mbps link, which clean_link covers at full length. The scenarios exist for the fix-record check (#594).

Not comparable: `host_rtt` (a host RTT 75.8 ms short of the int64 limit from 8 s) is ours only; sm_compare's libwebrtc side ignores it, as it does #441's host_rtt_inf, so libwebrtc runs this link with its measured RTT. The scenario exists for the UBSan overflow on the base (#451). With per_stream_rtt on (#568) the host value no longer reaches the send streams' periodic update, so most cells fall within the band; the near-limit RTT still reaches AimdRateControl's near-max increase.

D3 closed (#732): in band at #479's re-measure on main b48b3d8 and on main's 10 seeds since (freeze total 424 vs 1379 within the band; e2e p95 206 vs 219; render fps 29.8 vs 29.8).
